belief: A join returns as many rows as the left table has.
correction: A join returns one row per matching pair, so one left row can appear many times.

belief: count(*) after a join counts orders.
correction: count(*) counts result rows, which are order and item pairs.

belief: A join stacks the rows of both tables.
correction: A join pairs rows side by side; a union stacks them.

belief: SQL runs top to bottom in the order it is written.
correction: The database runs FROM first and SELECT near the end.

belief: An alias defined in SELECT can be used in WHERE.
correction: WHERE runs before SELECT, so the alias does not exist yet.

belief: LIMIT 10 without ORDER BY returns the first ten rows inserted.
correction: Without ORDER BY the row order is not defined and can change between runs.

belief: NULL = NULL is true.
correction: The result is unknown, so WHERE drops the row; use IS NULL.

belief: WHERE x <> 5 also returns rows where x is NULL.
correction: NULL <> 5 is unknown, so those rows are dropped.

belief: NULL is the same as 0 or an empty string.
correction: NULL means no known value; it is not equal to anything, not even to 0.

belief: GROUP BY returns the groups sorted by key.
correction: The order of groups is not defined; add ORDER BY.

belief: WHERE sum(total) > 100 filters groups.
correction: WHERE runs before grouping and cannot see aggregates; use HAVING.

belief: With GROUP BY you can select any column.
correction: A selected column must be in GROUP BY or inside an aggregate, because a bucket has many values for it.

belief: count(column) counts rows like count(*).
correction: It skips rows where the column is NULL.

belief: A float column is fine for prices.
correction: Floating point cannot store 0.1 exactly; use numeric or integer cents.

belief: Validation in the application is enough; the database just stores.
correction: Other writers, scripts and bugs bypass the app, so constraints are the last line of defense.

belief: A natural value such as an email is a good primary key.
correction: Natural values change, and every foreign key copying it must change too.

belief: The foreign key goes on the table that is the one in one-to-many.
correction: It goes on the many side, because a single column holds one value.

belief: A many-to-many relation can be a list of ids in one column.
correction: A list column cannot be checked by a foreign key; use a junction table.

belief: Deleting a parent row silently deletes its children.
correction: By default the delete fails; cascading must be requested with ON DELETE CASCADE.

belief: Adding WHERE on the right table of a LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched left rows.
correction: The NULL-filled rows fail the condition and vanish; put it in ON.

belief: Duplicated data is fine because the code updates all copies.
correction: Any missed update or crash leaves the copies different.

belief: One wide table is simpler than several small ones.
correction: It is simpler to read and harder to change correctly.

belief: More indexes always make the database faster.
correction: Each index slows writes and uses space, and many are never used.

belief: If an index exists, the database uses it.
correction: The planner uses it only when it estimates a lower cost than a scan.

belief: An index makes any slow query fast.
correction: It helps queries that select few rows by the indexed value, not those that read most of the table.

belief: Two statements in a row run as one unit.
correction: Another session can run between them; only a transaction groups them.

belief: Reading a balance and then writing the new balance is safe.
correction: Another session can change the row between the read and the write.

belief: BEGIN locks the whole database for other sessions.
correction: Only rows touched for writing, or locked on purpose, block others.

belief: ROLLBACK can undo a transaction that already committed.
correction: After COMMIT the change is durable; only uncommitted work can be rolled back.

belief: A deadlock hangs the database until someone restarts it.
correction: PostgreSQL detects the cycle and aborts one transaction with an error.

belief: Row locks are released when the statement finishes.
correction: They are held until COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

belief: A SELECT alias cannot be used in ORDER BY.
correction: ORDER BY runs after SELECT, so it can use the alias.

belief: LIMIT cuts the first rows, then WHERE filters them.
correction: WHERE runs first; ORDER BY and LIMIT work on the rows that survived it.

belief: WHERE can filter on aggregates because it runs after GROUP BY.
correction: WHERE runs before GROUP BY, so it never sees a sum; use HAVING for groups.

belief: HAVING filters single rows before they are grouped.
correction: HAVING runs after GROUP BY and filters whole groups.

belief: If one side of an OR is NULL, the whole OR is NULL.
correction: Unknown OR true is true; only unknown OR false stays unknown.
